narrative: Material PL1__M5731C2D exhibits lumpy, high-variability demand (CV=0.827) across 209 working days, with a mean of 66.92 units/day and frequent zero-demand periods. Lead times are highly variable (CV=0.683, range 0.12–3.37 days), requiring a conservative effective lead time of 2.63 days. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy is recommended with safety stock raised from 125 to 164 units to achieve 95% service level. The EOQ of ~3,980 units is capacity-capped to 3,948 units, consolidating replenishments from frequent small MOQ orders into ~4 annual orders, reducing total annual cost by 74%.
warnings: Storage capacity constraint is binding: order quantity capped at 3948 (from unconstrained 3980) to satisfy max_storage_units=4112.256 with safety_stock=164.
High demand variability detected (CV=0.827): lumpy demand regime; safety stock raised above SAP baseline.
High lead time variability (CV=0.683): variable supplier performance increases stockout exposure.
Recommended safety stock (164) exceeds current SAP setting (125): ERP parameters require update.

research_insights.selection_rationale: With lumpy but non-intermittent demand (non-zero fraction 75%) and variable lead times, a continuous-review (r,Q) policy provides tight stockout control by triggering a fixed replenishment order whenever inventory falls to the reorder point. This is preferable to periodic review given the high demand and lead-time variability, and EOQ provides the cost-optimal batch size.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity constraint binds at 4,112 units. The EOQ-derived unconstrained order of 3,980 units + safety stock 164 = 4,144 units exceeds capacity by 32 units. The order quantity has been reduced to 3,948 units (capacity floor). This marginally reduces cycle efficiency but remains well above MOQ=500. No material service level impact expected.
